original_question: Which pairs of polytopes P and Q have a nonempty amalgamation class hP, Qi for which the number of flag orbits among polytopes in hP, Qi is bounded?
target_in_paper: The open problem in the paper’s amalgamation discussion asking for a characterization of those pairs of abstract polytopes P and Q for which the amalgamation class <P,Q>, when nonempty, has a uniform upper bound on the number of flag-orbits of its members.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content of the paper’s target problem: it is about amalgamation classes <P,Q>, assumes nonemptiness of that class, and asks for a uniform bound on the number of flag-orbits among polytopes in the class. It also correctly focuses on pairs (P,Q), rather than on a single polytope or on a broader realization/classification problem.
missing_details: The paper is about abstract polytopes, not necessarily convex or geometric polytopes.
P and Q should be of compatible rank; in the standard amalgamation setting they are abstract n-polytopes and members of <P,Q> are abstract (n+1)-polytopes.
The compatibility condition underlying amalgamation should be stated: the vertex-figures of P must be isomorphic to the facets of Q.
The notation <P,Q> should be defined explicitly as the class of all abstract polytopes whose facets are isomorphic to P and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to Q.
The phrase 'number of flag orbits' should be made explicit as the number of orbits of flags under the full automorphism group of the polytope.
The boundedness quantifier should be stated precisely: there exists an integer k=k(P,Q) such that every polytope R in <P,Q> has at most k flag-orbits.
It should be made explicit that the question is only about those pairs (P,Q) for which <P,Q> is nonempty.
No extra finiteness assumption should be inserted unless the paper explicitly imposes one; your draft leaves this implicit.
refined_question: Let P and Q be compatible abstract n-polytopes, meaning that each vertex-figure of P is isomorphic to each facet of Q, and let <P,Q> denote the class of all abstract (n+1)-polytopes whose facets are isomorphic to P and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to Q. Assuming <P,Q> is nonempty, for which pairs (P,Q) does there exist a constant k=k(P,Q) such that every polytope R in <P,Q> has at most k flag-orbits under its full automorphism group?
justification: The draft is already close to the paper’s intended open problem, but it is not fully stand-alone. The paper’s formulation lives in the abstract-polytope amalgamation setting, so the refined version restores the ambient category, the rank shift from P and Q to members of <P,Q>, the compatibility condition hidden in the amalgamation notation, and the exact quantifier behind 'bounded'. This keeps the question as narrow as the paper’s intent: it does not broaden to arbitrary realization, extension, or classification problems, and it does not replace the bounded-orbit question by the broader existence problem for amalgamations.
